title: Initiating a project: practices applied and judging the process
blurb: Say which practice each initiation action applies, and judge whether initiation builds solid, proportionate foundations in the scenario.
question: During initiation the project manager develops the product breakdown structure, work breakdown structure and product flow diagram. Which practice is being applied, and is the initiation effective?

teach.h: What initiation builds, and how to judge it
teach.body: Formally: initiating a project applies the practices to build the PID (tab 15.3), and is judged against its purpose of solid foundations before significant expenditure, its objectives, tailoring and roles (15.1 to 15.7). In plain English: name the practice behind each initiation product, then ask whether the work gives the board a clear, consistent and proportionate basis to commit money, without starting delivery early.

head: Practice
What initiation does
Product
rows: Develops the PBS, WBS and product flow diagram
Develops the issue approach; sets up the issue register
Updates the project management team structure
Develops the outline into the full business case
Agree their approaches; registers set up
Agrees controls and the digital and data approach
teach.caption: The first four rows are the official tab 15.3 extracts the exam uses most. The others follow from where each approach sits.

teach.body: Initiation exists so the business understands the work needed to deliver the project product before committing significant money or resources. Its objectives are a common understanding of the reasons, benefits and risks; scope and products; how, when and at what cost they are delivered; who decides; how quality, baselines, risks, issues and progress are controlled; who needs what information; and how business policies apply.

teach.h: How the full business case is built

root.label: How big and risky is the project?

items: Purpose: does the action help the board understand the work before major spend?
Timing: is it initiation work, or delivery work started before authorization?
Fit: do the approaches reflect business standards, the PPD and lessons from similar projects?
Consistency: is the PID cross-checked and baselined?
Proportion: is the tailoring suited to the project's size, risk and team?

teach.body: In Fernhollow's four-week initiation, Nadia Osei builds the product breakdown and work breakdown structures, showing which supplier delivers what. She sets up the issue register and agrees how requests for extra recipes will be handled. She writes a commercial approach for the design agency, line supplier and co-manufacturer, and adds the line supplier's engineer to the team structure. A sustainability approach controls the 1.5 kg carbon target. Packaging design waits for the next stage.

teach.text: Classic traps: initiation is NOT the time to start designing or building products; that waits for authorization. Using the project plan's figures in the business case is still the business case practice, not plans. A sustainability target needs its own controls in the sustainability management approach, even if a carbon label appears on the pack.

items: Tab 15.3: plans (PBS, WBS, product flow diagram), issues (issue approach, register), organizing (PMT structure), business case (outline to full).
Commercial approach: organizing; digital and data approach: progress; sustainability approach: business case.
Purpose: solid foundations before significant spend.
Judge by purpose, timing, fit, consistency and proportion.

summary: You can now name the practice behind each initiation action, including where each management approach sits. You can also judge whether initiation is effective and proportionate: foundations before spend, approaches that fit, a cross-checked PID and no delivery work started early.

A.q: Fernhollow Foods is initiating its Fernhollow Kitchen project. The project manager develops a product breakdown structure for the six meals, packaging and new line, a work breakdown structure and a product flow diagram. Which practice is being applied?
options: Organizing, because the WBS shows how teams are structured
Quality, because each product will need a description
Plans, because it develops the PBS, WBS and flow diagram
Progress, because the flow diagram sets the stage reviews
A.why: Tab 15.3: plans is applied in initiating a project by developing the product breakdown structure, work breakdown structure and product flow diagram.

whyNot.0: The WBS helps structure teams, but developing these planning products is listed under plans.
whyNot.1: Product descriptions are quality-related, but the action here is product-based planning.
whyNot.3: The flow diagram shows product sequence, not progress reviews.

A.q: During Fernhollow's initiation, the project manager sets up the issue register and agrees how requests for change, such as the request for extra recipes, will be captured, assessed and decided. Which practice is being applied?
options: Issues, because it develops the issue approach and register
Risk, because extra recipes could threaten the launch date
Plans, because changes alter the project plan baseline
Business case, because extra recipes change the benefits
A.why: Tab 15.3: issues is applied in initiating a project by developing the issue management approach and setting up the issue register.

whyNot.1: Extra recipes might create risk, but the action here is setting up issue and change control.
whyNot.2: A change may alter a baseline, but the procedure for handling it is the issues practice.
whyNot.3: The business case may be affected by a change, but the action is setting up issue handling.

A.q: In Fernhollow's initiation, the project manager adds the Dutch line supplier's project engineer as a team manager for installation and updates the project management team structure chart. Which practice is being applied?
options: Plans, because the engineer will produce the line products
Issues, because a new team manager changes a baseline
Quality, because the engineer will commission the line
Organizing, because it updates the team structure
A.why: Tab 15.3: organizing is applied in initiating a project by updating the project management team structure.

whyNot.0: The engineer will deliver products, but updating the PMT structure is organizing.
whyNot.1: The structure is being completed in initiation, not changed through issue control.
whyNot.2: Commissioning involves quality checks, but the action here is updating the team structure.

B.q: Fernhollow's project manager updates the outline business case with the £2.3 million cost and timescales from the project plan and the aggregated risks from the project log, ready for the board. Which practice is being applied?
options: Plans, because it uses time and cost from the project plan
Business case, because the outline becomes the full case
Risk, because it brings together the aggregated risks
Progress, because it sets the cost baseline to track
B.why: Tab 15.3: business case is applied in initiating a project by developing the outline business case into a full business case for board approval.

whyNot.0: The figures come from the plan, but developing the business case is the business case practice.
whyNot.2: Aggregated risks are an input; the product being developed is the business case.
whyNot.3: Progress later tracks against baselines; this action builds the justification.

B.q: Fernhollow's finance director is worried about the co-manufacturer's 150,000-meal minimum. In initiation, the project manager sets out responsibilities and resources for procurement and contract management, and which parts of the work each external supplier delivers. Which practice is being applied?
options: Risk, because the minimum volume is a threat to cash flow
Business case, because contract costs affect the benefits
Plans, because supplier work appears in the WBS
Organizing, because this is the commercial approach
B.why: The commercial management approach, covering market engagement, procurement, contract management and the delivery model, belongs to the organizing practice (6.5, 6.3.2.1).

whyNot.0: The minimum volume is a risk to record, but setting out commercial responsibilities is the commercial approach.
whyNot.1: Costs feed the business case, but how contracts are managed is organizing.
whyNot.2: The WBS shows supplier work, but responsibilities for procurement and contracts are the commercial approach.

B.q: During Fernhollow's initiation, the project manager defines how recipe trial data and consumer panel results will be stored, kept secure, accessed and retained during and after the project. Which practice is being applied?
options: Progress, because this is the digital and data approach
Quality, because trial results show products meet criteria
Risk, because a data breach would harm the business
Issues, because data errors would need to be resolved
B.why: The digital and data management approach sits under the progress practice; it covers how data is created, used and managed, including security, access and retention (11.5).

whyNot.1: Trial results are quality records, but deciding how data is managed is the digital and data approach.
whyNot.2: A breach would be a risk, but the action is defining data management.
whyNot.3: Errors may become issues, but the action defines how data is handled.

C.q: Fernhollow's four-week initiation is under way. To save time, the project manager asks the design agency to start detailed artwork for the packaging sleeves before the board has authorized the project. Is this an appropriate way to carry out initiation, and why?
options: Yes, because packaging must be recyclable at the kerbside
Yes, because the launch week in February cannot move
No, because delivery work waits until the project is authorized
No, because the design agency should approve its own sleeve designs
C.why: Initiation builds foundations so the business understands the work before committing significant spend; the project should be properly initiated and authorized before delivery work starts (15.1, 2.4).

whyNot.0: Recyclability is a requirement, but it does not justify starting delivery before authorization.
whyNot.1: A fixed date adds pressure, but committing spend before authorization undermines initiation's purpose.
whyNot.3: Who approves the designs is set in product descriptions; the real problem is starting before authorization.

C.q: During Fernhollow's initiation, the managing director says a separate sustainability management approach is unnecessary because each pack will carry a carbon label. The board wants packs recyclable at the kerbside and no more than 1.5 kg CO2e per meal. Is it appropriate to drop the approach, and why?
options: Yes, because the carbon label is a quality specification
Yes, because tailoring lets the PM drop or merge approaches
No, because it sets controls for the sustainability targets
No, because all nine approaches must be separate documents
C.why: The sustainability management approach defines the actions, reviews and controls needed to achieve the project's sustainability performance targets (ch 5).

whyNot.0: The label is a product feature; the targets still need actions, reviews and controls.
whyNot.1: Approaches can be merged when tailoring, but dropping controls for real targets leaves them unmanaged.
whyNot.3: Approaches can be combined in or alongside the PID; they need not be separate documents.

C.q: Before requesting authorization, Fernhollow's project manager checks that the factory trial dates in the project plan match the audit timing in the quality management approach, and that the communication approach covers the supermarket buyer. Is this an appropriate application of the 'assemble the project initiation documentation' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the PID's parts are cross-checked for compatibility
Yes, because the PID is baselined once the project is closed
No, because cross-checking the PID is project assurance's task
No, because the board checks the PID's consistency when authorizing it
C.why: Assembling the PID includes a cross-check of the information in its parts to ensure they are compatible (15.4.6).

whyNot.1: The PID is baselined when used to gain authorization, not at closure.
whyNot.2: Assurance may review, but the cross-check is part of the PM's assembly of the PID.
whyNot.3: The board reviews the PID, but the PM is expected to check consistency before asking.

reteach.title: Initiation products and their practices
reteach.question: Can you match each initiation product to its practice and spot initiation that goes too far?

blocks.body: Breakdowns and flow diagrams: plans. Issue approach and register: issues. Team structure and commercial approach: organizing. Full business case and sustainability approach: business case. Data approach and controls: progress. Then ask whether the work stays as foundations or slips into delivery.

head: Initiation product
Practice
rows: Project controls, digital and data approach

blocks.text: Initiation that designs or builds products is not 'ahead of schedule': it commits spend before the board has authorized the project.

explain.body: Plans is applied by developing the product breakdown structure, work breakdown structure and product flow diagram for the project plan. Issues is applied by developing the issue management approach and setting up the issue register.

test.q: Fernhollow's project manager sets up the issue register during initiation. Which practice does this apply?
options: Risk
Progress
Quality
Issues
test.why: Tab 15.3: issues is applied in initiating a project by developing the issue management approach and setting up the issue register.

whyNot.0: Risk has its own register and approach.
whyNot.2: Quality has its own register for quality activities.

explain.body: Organizing is applied by updating the project management team structure, and the commercial approach sits in this practice. Business case is applied by developing the outline business case into the full business case, using the plan's time and cost and the aggregated risks.

head: Practice
Initiation product
rows: Full business case; benefits and sustainability approaches

test.q: Fernhollow's project manager writes the approach for securing and managing the contracts with the design agency, line supplier and co-manufacturer. Which practice does this approach belong to?
options: Plans
Organizing
Business case
Risk
test.why: The commercial management approach belongs to the organizing practice (6.5).

whyNot.0: Plans covers the breakdown structures and plans.
whyNot.2: Business case holds the benefits and sustainability approaches.
whyNot.3: Risk holds the risk management approach.

explain.body: Quality approach: quality. Risk approach: risk. Digital and data approach: progress. Benefits and sustainability approaches: business case. Change and communication approaches: the people element. All are agreed in 'agree the management approaches'.

test.q: Fernhollow's board wants every pack to stay under 1.5 kg CO2e per meal. In which practice's management approach should the actions, reviews and controls for this target sit?
options: Quality
Progress
Business case
Organizing
test.why: The sustainability management approach belongs to the business case practice and defines the actions, reviews and controls for sustainability targets (ch 5).

whyNot.0: The quality approach covers quality planning, control and assurance.
whyNot.1: Progress holds the digital and data approach.
whyNot.3: Organizing holds the commercial management approach.

explain.body: Effective initiation gives the board a cross-checked, baselined PID before significant spend. It fails if it starts delivery early, leaves targets without controls, over-engineers a small project or skips lessons on the approaches.

test.q: Fernhollow's initiation produced a PID whose project plan, quality approach and communication approach were cross-checked, and the version used for authorization was baselined. How well was initiation carried out?
options: Well, because it gives a consistent baseline for the board
Well, because baselining lets the PM change it freely later
Poorly, because the PID should be baselined at closure
Poorly, because cross-checks belong to the board's decision
test.why: Cross-checking makes the parts compatible, and baselining the authorized version puts it under change control (15.4.6).

whyNot.1: Baselining places the PID under change control, so changes are controlled, not free.
whyNot.2: The PID is baselined when used to gain authorization.
whyNot.3: The PM cross-checks the PID while assembling it, before the board decides.
